- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) or flat (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk-off or mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- Model shows strong lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns negative within 3 days, forecast should be adjusted downward by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: if model is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid over-reliance on recent high volatility; use 14-day EWMA to filter noise and anchor forecast near 10-day moving average.
